item.title: Problem-Driven Innovation in Genome Editing: From Programmable Nucleases to DSB-Free Precision Editors and the Path to Clinical Translation.
item.abstract: Precise, heritable modification of living genomes is among the most consequential advances in modern biology, offering the prospect of correcting molecular lesions underlying monogenic diseases. Realizing this potential has required successive rounds of innovation, in which each generation of tools addressed limitations while revealing new constraints. This Review traces that trajectory through a problem-driven lens, from programmable nucleases to RNA-guided systems and double-strand break (DSB)-avoiding precision editors. Zinc-finger nucleases and TALENs established programmable DSB induction, whereas CRISPR-Cas9 simplified retargeting through an RNA guide but retained DSB-associated risks, including stochastic indels, large deletions, and chromosomal rearrangements. Base and prime editors avoid programmed DSBs but are not consequence-free: Most base editors use Cas9 nickase and can generate bystander editing, off-target deamination, and low-frequency indels, whereas prime editing also uses nicked intermediates and remains sensitive to endogenous repair, editor architecture, and locus-specific efficiency. Clinical programs likewise use distinct mechanisms. Exagamglogene autotemcel (Casgevy) is an ex vivo SpCas9-ribonucleoprotein therapy in autologous HSPCs that disrupts the BCL11A erythroid enhancer through nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ)-dominated DSB repair; NTLA-2001 is an in vivo liver-directed lipid nanoparticle (LNP) therapy that codelivers Cas9 mRNA and a TTR-targeting guide RNA for NHEJ-mediated gene disruption; and VERVE programs deliver adenine base editor mRNA with a PCSK9-targeting guide RNA in LNPs for targeted base conversion. Translational constraints now include efficient and safe delivery, particularly beyond the liver and ex vivo-accessible cell populations, immunogenicity, long-term genomic safety, manufacturing scalability, and equitable access. Resolving these challenges will determine the ultimate clinical impact of genome editing on human health.

item.title: A High-Efficiency In Vivo Continuous Evolution Platform for Antiviral Peptides Engineering.
item.abstract: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is an ideal host for protein evolution, but the low efficiency of CRISPR-guided EvolvR systems has limited targeted continuous mutagenesis in yeast. Here, we developed an enhanced yeast EvolvR platform, eyEvolvR, by combining local recruitment of an error-prone DNA polymerase, suppression of mismatch repair, and multiplex sgRNA co-targeting. These synergistic optimizations increased the on-target mutation rate by up to ∼500-fold relative to the original yeast EvolvR system. To demonstrate its utility, we applied eyEvolvR to the continuous evolution of the antiviral peptide LCB1 against the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron EG.5 variant. Iterative rounds of mutagenesis and selection generated LCB1 variants with substantially improved binding to the EG.5 receptor-binding domain. A multivalent construct based on the top evolved variant potently neutralized both EG.5 and JN.1 pseudoviruses. These results establish eyEvolvR as an efficient platform for continuous in vivo protein evolution in yeast.

item.title: flexiAsCas12a and other Cas12a variants enhance the applicability of Cas12a nucleases in prime editing.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amongst the genome manipulation tools based on the versatile CRISPR-Cas system, prime editing is the most prominent one as a method that enables precise insertions, deletions, and substitutions without inducing double-strand breaks. Cas12a nucleases are widely used for genome editing and nucleic acid detection, owing to their unique properties; however, their relatively long PAM requirements limit their applicability.
RESULTS: We develop PAM-flexible Cas12a variants capable of functioning effectively within mammalian cells, thereby enabling the cleavage of targets previously inaccessible to Cas12a nucleases. Amongst the Lb-, As-, Mb-, and FnCas12a variants we develop, flexiAsCas12a (AsCas12a with flexible PAM recognition) is the most effective, expanding the range of recognized PAM sequences by Cas12a variants to include NATN, NCCN and GTCN sequences. Using the currently available Cas12a variants with relaxed PAM recognition (impLbCas12a, flexiAsCas12a, and enAsCas12a), we develop circular RNA-guided split prime editors and validate their functionality on non-canonical PAM sequences.
CONCLUSIONS: flexiAsCas12a joins the repertoire of Cas12a PAM variants, enabling access to an increasing number of target sequences by Cas12a nucleases.

item.title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states.
item.abstract: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes in the absence of signaling partners or mimetics has proven challenging. Here we show that by combining generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction we can reliably design fiducial markers to facilitate cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points, enabling the visualization of previously intractable states. We validate the approach with high-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs, allowing for key details of receptor pharmacology to be resolved in each case. We then engineered an extracellular fiducial marker for the prototypical β2-adrenergic receptor that enabled direct structural characterization of the rearrangement of key intracellular motifs in the absence of G-protein. Comparison with recent co-folding models highlights major gaps in current methods for predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations. These results present a generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Design of Peptides with Custom Secondary Structure Motifs and Reduced Amino Acid Alphabets.
item.abstract: Proteins are highly diverse functional polymers where the specific sequence of amino acids, selected from a standard genetically encoded alphabet of 20 (C20), determines the structure and ultimately the function of the resulting folded protein. This standard alphabet has been identified to be nonrandomly distributed in physicochemical properties crucial to both structure formation and function, often referred to as coverage theory. While machine learning models have drastically improved protein structure prediction, success of protein design models lags structure prediction, particularly for custom secondary structure motifs and amino acid alphabets. Here, we therefore bridge contemporary biological theory with recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) to develop and evaluate a generative AI protein design model, trained on hundreds of thousands of proteins within the RCSB PDB, for custom secondary structure motifs using reduced amino acid alphabets (RAAs). Results indicate an overall success in designing novel proteins with desired secondary structure motifs for a broad range of amino acid alphabets and complexity of designs. Interestingly, for a substantial fraction of designs, ESMFold predicts a fold close to that of the target structure despite training only on physicochemical sequence space and secondary structure information. The development of this model advances research across multiple disciplines, from general scientific AI architecture development to protein design for biotechnology, astrobiology, and early-Earth evolutionary biology.

item.title: Advances in genome editing techniques of non-model microorganisms for next-generation cell factories in synthetic biology.
item.abstract: Non-model microorganisms with innate traits such as extremophile, alternative carbon utilization, or specialized metabolism are emerging as attractive industrial chassis for the next-generation cell factories in synthetic biology. Their exploitation, however, remains constrained by the lack of efficient genetic editing toolkits. We delineate the evolution of genetic engineering technologies across diverse non-model hosts, including probiotics, carbon-utilizing bacteria, and extremophiles, based on available one-strain-one-strategy research. Although effective for many individual species, this approach faces fundamental scalability limits, underscoring broader future strategies. The review further summarizes three cross-cutting barriers that impede genetic engineering (the cell envelope/host defense systems, DNA repair limitations, and genetic tool compatibility), outlining targeted strategies to overcome each barrier. Computational strategies have been proposed to complement empirical tool development, as substantial data generation and validation are still needed before such approaches can be broadly applied. To support this direction, we propose a conceptual framework that links systematic data collection with computationally informed tool matching, which could guide better tool development decisions for diverse non-model chassis.

item.title: Design of mini-protein binders targeting CD46 to enhance complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
item.abstract: The complement system exhibits a typical dual regulatory role. Aberrant activation of the complement system contributes to the development of autoimmune diseases, whereas excessive suppression of complement facilitates tumor progression. Cancer cells evade complement-mediated killing by overexpressing three key complement regulatory proteins, CD46, CD55, and CD59. Among them, CD46 has attracted substantial research attention owing to its marked overexpression in a range of hematological malignancies and solid tumors. By overexpressing CD46, cancer cells promote the degradation of C3b and C4b, thereby escaping complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC). CD46 ectodomain consists of four small complement control protein (CCP) domains, which provide a limited interfacial area for molecular interaction, posing certain challenges for binder design. In this study, we integrated deep learning-based backbone generation, sequence design, and complex structure prediction to design and screen a panel of mini-protein binders targeting the complement-binding domain of CD46. We further optimized the binding affinity of the lead mini-protein binder via the partial diffusion strategy, achieving a final affinity of 287.5 pM. CDC assays showed that the monomeric mini-protein binder and the trimeric affinity-optimized viral ligand Ad35K++ exhibit similar potency for enhancing rituximab (RTX)-mediated CDC effect. Biochemical experiments confirmed that the engineered mini-protein binder exhibits high binding specificity for CD46 and good thermal stability. In conclusion, these newly designed mini-protein binders show promise for further pharmaceutical development and clinical translation.

item.title: Metabolic engineering of Escherichia coli for the de novo production of 1,6-hexamethylenediamine from glucose.
item.abstract: 1,6-Hexamethylenediamine (HMD) is a critical monomer for the production of nylon 66. However, its direct fermentative production from renewable carbon sources is strongly hindered by the lack of native biosynthetic pathways. In this study, we established a complete de novo HMD production platform in Escherichia coli by designing and systematically optimizing an artificial adipoyl-CoA-dependent pathway. To eliminate major upstream bottlenecks, an efficient eukaryotic enoyl-CoA reductase (CthETR) was identified, and peripheral competitive nodes were disrupted to maximize precursor flux. For the downstream cascade, a high-performance acylating aldehyde dehydrogenase from Acidaminococcus massiliensis (AmAldDH) was selected to drive direct reduction of adipyl-CoA, while deletion of the endogenous alcohol dehydrogenase yqhD blocked alcohol byproduct diversion, elevating amination selectivity by over 94.5%. Multi-plasmid metabolic burden was mitigated via multi-copy chromosomal integration of upstream modules, coupled with the coordinated reinforcement of intracellular NADPH and CoA pools. Furthermore, directed evolution of the rate-limiting enzyme AmAldDH yielded a superior variant (A405G) with a 1.6-fold increase in specific activity. The resulting engineered strain achieved an HMD titer of 0.83 g/L in shake flasks and 2.41 g/L in fed-batch fermentation with a yield of 0.07 g/g glucose, representing the highest de novo HMD titer reported to date. This work provides a promising biological route towards the sustainable manufacturing of nylon 66.

item.title: Biological oscillations without intracellular oscillator or external forcing.
item.abstract: Spontaneous biological oscillations are typically attributed to specific architectures within metabolic or gene regulatory networks. Here, we uncover a more general mechanism arising from the interplay between cellular growth, burdensome gene expression, and nutrient availability, which can generate oscillations in both growth and gene expression. Focusing on sporulation dynamics in Bacillus subtilis, we developed a minimal model that captures these coupled processes and analytically identified the range of continuous culture conditions that give rise to oscillatory behavior. These predictions were experimentally validated in chemostat cultures. Our results demonstrate that oscillations can emerge independently of specific genetic circuit architectures, and without external forcing. More broadly, they reveal that feedback between environmental conditions and cellular states is sufficient to drive oscillatory dynamics, suggesting that such behavior may be widespread in long-term cultivation systems where gene expression, growth, and resource availability are tightly coupled.

item.title: Gene Therapy for Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type I: Current Advances, Clinical Translation, and Future Perspectives.
item.abstract: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is a group of rare autosomal recessive primary immunodeficiencies characterized by impaired leukocyte migration resulting from defective expression or function of adhesion molecules. The most common and severe form, LAD-I, is caused by biallelic mutations in Integrin Subunit Beta 2 (ITGB2), which encodes the β2-integrin subunit CD18, leading to recurrent life-threatening infections and impaired wound healing. LAD-II arises from mutations in the fucose-metabolism gene SLC35C1, and LAD-III from mutations in FERMT3, which disrupt integrin activation through kindlin-3. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) has historically been the only established curative treatment for severe LAD-I, but donor availability, conditioning toxicity, and graft-versus-host disease limit its use and have motivated the development of autologous approaches. Autologous gene therapy using self-inactivating lentiviral vectors to introduce functional ITGB2 into patient-derived hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells has shown promising clinical results, including restored CD18 expression, improved leukocyte function, and fewer severe infections. In March 2026, the FDA granted accelerated approval to marnetegragene autotemcel (Kresladi; RP-L201), making it the first approved gene therapy for severe LAD-I in the United States. CRISPR/Cas9, base editing, and prime editing are also being investigated as alternative approaches for correcting ITGB2 mutations, although their application in LAD-I remains preclinical. These methods could allow correction of pathogenic ITGB2 variants without relying on integrating viral vectors, but their efficacy and long-term safety in LAD-I have yet to be established. However, conditioning-related toxicity, the need for long-term safety monitoring, and the complexity and cost of manufacturing remain important limitations to wider clinical use. This review examines the molecular basis of LAD, preclinical and clinical studies of gene therapy for LAD-I, and the challenges that remain in translating genome-editing approaches into clinical practice.

item.title: Discovery and Functional Characterization of Salinity-Responsive Promoters in Pseudomonas putida KT2440.
item.abstract: While microbial bioprocesses offer environmental advantages, their reliance on freshwater remains a significant challenge. Seawater presents a sustainable alternative; however, its high salinity often limits microbial growth and survival. This study aimed to identify salt stress-responsive biological parts for microbial engineering in the versatile synthetic biology chassis Pseudomonas putida KT2440. Using available transcriptomic data, we identified intergenic regions upstream of genes consistently upregulated under saline and other industrially relevant conditions. These regions were cloned into a reporter plasmid and functionally evaluated in KT2440. We characterized two novel salt-inducible promoters: PPP_1833 and PPP_4707. Compared to standard media, supplementation with 3.5% (w/v) NaCl increased their integrated fluorescence by 4.9-fold and 8.5-fold, respectively. Furthermore, both promoters maintained robust activity in an artificial seawater-based medium. Conversely, neither promoter showed activity in Escherichia coli DH10B under identical conditions, highlighting species-specific regulatory differences in salinity response. These findings introduce two new salt-responsive regulatory elements in P. putida KT2440, expanding the genetic toolkit for optimizing bioprocesses in saline environments.

item.title: A cell-free ERRγ-TOXICITY biosensor mimicking the nuclear receptor/coactivator interaction for the rapid detection of ERRγ-disrupting effects.
item.abstract: Environmental chemicals can exert estrogenic effects by disrupting the transcriptional activity of estrogen-related receptor γ (ERRγ). Detection of the estrogenic effects of environmental chemicals acting on ERRγ is of great significance for assessing their endocrine disruption toxicity. The present work developed a new type of biosensor named "ERRγ-TOXICITY biosensor", which measures the inhibition of chemicals on ERRγ activity by mimicking ERRγ/coactivator interaction in a cell-free system. Unlike conventional biosensors, the core of this toxicity biosensor is the use of ERRγ as the effective biomarker, and it can therefore identify all ERRγ antagonists, not just a single one. The biosensor was constructed with the activated ERRγ as the target, a carboxyfluorescein-labeled coactivator peptide as the recognition element, and fluorescence anisotropy as the signal transduction mechanism. An ERRγ antagonist induces ERRγ into the inactive state, leading to the dissociation of the receptor/peptide complex and a decrease in fluorescence anisotropy. The developed biosensor exhibited a half-maximal effective concentration of 20.3 nM for 4-hydroxytamoxifen (an ERRγ antagonist) and a detection limit of 0.6 nM. No response was observed with the agonist GSK4716, showing high selectivity toward ERRγ activity. The antagonistic activity of the five organophosphate esters evaluated by the biosensor followed the order of TCRP > TPHP > TDCP > EHDPP > TCPP, and the activity was also detected with concentrated tap water. Both results are consistent with cell-based assays, demonstrating the high reliability of the biosensor. The biosensor overcomes the limitations of animal and cell assay toxicity testing with fast response, simple operation, low cost, and high reproducibility.

item.title: Visualizing Hidden Cellular Consequences of Infection by a Minimal Genome Virus.
item.abstract: Circoviruses represent an extreme of genome compression among animal viruses and infect diverse vertebrate hosts, including humans. Porcine circovirus 2 (PCV2) combines an exceptionally compact genome, well-established pathogenicity, and routine propagation in cultured cells, making it a practical model for studying minimal-genome virus infection. Here, we engineered a compact tetracysteine (TC)-FlAsH reporter by optimizing TC placement and configuration within the PCV2 capsid. The resulting PCV2-TC remained replication competent and enabled direct visualization and longitudinal tracking of infected cells. The reporter resolved apoptosis-associated fate transitions in living cells and enabled ultrastructural analysis of reporter-positive cells. It further uncovered Annexin V and propidium iodide (PI)-defined cell states that were masked in population-level analysis. Together, this system establishes PCV2 as a tractable minimal-genome model for directly linking infection to cell fate and revealing cellular consequences otherwise obscured in bulk populations.

item.title: Indole-3-lactic acid from gut microbiota suppresses colorectal cancer through AHR-ZBP1 signaling and PANoptosis-like cell death.
item.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden. This study observed reduced relative abundance of sequences assigned to Roseburia inulinivorans in patients with CRC. R. inulinivorans-derived cell-free supernatant (CFS) reduced CRC cell viability and clonogenic capacity and decreased tumor burden in an azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium model. Metabolomic and functional screening prioritized indole-3-lactic acid (ILA) as a candidate metabolite. ILA increased ZBP1 expression, and AHR knockdown or inhibition attenuated this response. Chromatin accessibility, ChIP-qPCR, and promoter-reporter analyses supported AHR-associated regulation at the ZBP1 locus under ILA treatment. ILA increased signals associated with apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis, consistent with PANoptosis-like cell death. ZBP1 knockdown attenuated these responses, and intestinal epithelial Zbp1 deletion weakened the in vivo response to ILA. These findings identify ILA as a functional candidate metabolite and support a contribution of AHR-ZBP1 signaling to its antitumor activity and associated PANoptosis-like cell death in the tested CRC models.

cards.score_reason: 英伟达CEO人事重大变动

cards.one_liner: 英伟达宣布黄仁勋即刻复任总裁、CEO及董事会成员。
key_findings: 黄仁勋即刻恢复总裁、CEO及董事职务
公告由英伟达官方新闻室发布，未披露变动原因

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
item.abstract: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux. It helps teams protect running systems while they roll out patches.

cards.score_reason: OpenAI与思科开源运行时，值得关注
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 与 Cisco 推出开源 Linux 运行时 Shirudo
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 与 Cisco 发布开源 Linux 运行时 Shirudo，可在打补丁期间保护运行中的系统。
key_findings: Shirudo 是面向 Linux 的开源运行时，由 OpenAI 与 Cisco 联合推出。
核心用途是在团队部署补丁期间保护正在运行的系统。
开源形式便于团队集成到现有运维与安全流程。
cards.why_it_matters: 合成生物学实验室与生产环境大量依赖 Linux 服务器和自动化设备，补丁窗口期的系统防护可降低停机与安全风险，值得关注其落地方式。

item.title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days
item.abstract: Richpanel uses GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT-6 Luna for their conversations.

cards.score_reason: GPT-6系列模型应用，有参考价值
cards.title_cn: Richpanel 借助 GPT-6 系列模型，30 天内将企业客服自动化率提升至 50%
cards.one_liner: Richpanel 用 GPT-6 Astra、Sol、Luna 构建 AI 客服代理，30 天自动化 50% 支持工作。
key_findings: Astra 与 Sol 为 AI 客服代理提供工具和流程能力
Luna 专门负责对话交互环节
宣称 30 天内可自动化企业 50% 的客服工作量
cards.why_it_matters: 多模型分工（工具调用、流程执行、对话）是 AI 代理落地的工程范式，对合成生物学实验室自动化与 LIMS 智能助手设计有借鉴价值。

item.abstract: The new Asus ProArt laptop costs up to $7,000, but it can run a gaggle of local AI agents.

cards.score_reason: 本地AI笔记本评测，有参考价值
cards.title_cn: 评测：华硕 ProArt P16 展现本地 AI 驱动的未来雏形
cards.one_liner: 华硕 ProArt P16 售价最高 7000 美元，可本地运行多个 AI 智能体。
key_findings: 顶配售价达 7000 美元，定位高端创作与本地 AI 工作站。
可在本地同时运行多个 AI 智能体，无需依赖云端。
评测认为其展示了本地 AI 计算的未来方向。
cards.why_it_matters: 本地运行多智能体对合成生物学中的序列设计、文献挖掘等数据敏感场景有参考价值，但价格高昂，需评估性价比。

item.abstract: Using agent teams and formal verification to improve quantum algorithms for fusion and chemistry.

cards.score_reason: AI智能体量子算法，相关但偏门

cards.one_liner: Google DeepMind 用智能体团队加形式化验证，改进聚变与化学领域的量子算法。
key_findings: 以智能体团队自动搜索并优化量子算法，面向聚变与化学场景
引入形式化验证保证算法正确性，而非仅靠数值测试
属方法学进展，摘要未披露具体加速比或实验数据
cards.why_it_matters: 若方法可迁移，AI 加形式化验证或能加速量子算法设计；对合成生物学而言，化学模拟类量子算法值得关注，但当前与湿实验距离较远。
